messages:
nightly-bot: Nightly eval finished for rdx-alt-int6-v2 (02:13 UTC). medical-summaries prompt set shows a spike in hallucination rate: 4.2% (baseline 0.8%). Example and diff attached: https://go/report/2056789012 - regression after last quant sweep.

maya: Hmm. That's a pretty clear jump. Can someone paste the most illustrative sample here? @kevin @ali

kevin: Pasting one flagged example below — truncated patient note turned into a multipart invented history.
```
Prompt: "Pt c/o cough. CXR pending..."
Model gen (rdx-alt-int6-v2): "Pt c/o cough. CXR pending... Patient underwent coronary bypass in 2016, on clopidogrel, now awaiting transplant evaluation. Family history: father had early-onset Alzheimer's at 52."
Notes: the extra clinical history is fabricated and not present in the prompt. 
```

ali: I ran a quick local repro on the quant runner. Reproduces reliably on int6 and int8 builds, NOT on fp16. Kernel differences around softmax dequant look suspicious. Also see token-prob spikes at the ellipsis tokens.

lucy: We have 12 failing prompts flagged by the eval harness. Common pattern: short/incomplete notes ending with ellipses or trailing punctuation. Appears like the model expands the trailing tokens into long, coherent-looking histories.

sahil: Could be a rounding/noise amplification effect from quantization combined with attention position handling for short contexts. Suggest bisecting the quant kernel changes from the last sweep (commit abc123 -> def456). I can run a binary bisect tomorrow.

maya: Quick triage steps: 1) repro with temp=0.2 and temp=0.8; 2) try with kv-cache on/off; 3) compare logits for the ellipsis token and following tokens; 4) run a tiny batch of the failing prompts against rdx-alt-int6-v1 (previous) and v2. Please paste the exact command you run.

kevin: Running now. Command: `./tools/repro_eval.sh --model rdx-alt-int6-v2 --prompts datasets/medical-summaries/failing_list.txt --seed 42 --log-probs --temp 0.2` 
Starting with kv-cache=enabled; will toggle if needed. GPU: a100-80gb. ETA ~18m.

nightly-bot: Canary policy note: For hosted routes we will fallback to rdx-alt-fp16 if three consecutive nightly-eval blocks exceed the threshold. No live traffic triggered.

lucy: thx. once kevin posts logs I'll annotate the failing set and add to the regression ticket (REG-3219). :eyes:

maya: If anyone sees a quick fix (quant scaling tweak, reorder revert) that improves logits around punctuation, ping me. Otherwise leave the bisect to sahil and kevin.

kevin: Log excerpt (probabilities truncated):
```
Token: "..."  logit: -0.42  prob: 0.34
Next token: "Patient" logit: 1.6 prob: 0.70 (unexpectedly high)
```
Looks like the softmax mass concentrates after the ellipsis in the quant build. Sending full logs to REG-3219.

sahil: I'll start an A/B job comparing v1 vs v2 on the failing set and collect per-token KL and entropy. Will report back with links.

maya: good plan. marking this P1 for the bring-up team.

lucy: FYI i've already blocked exporting any of the flagged examples to analytic dashboards until we have a root cause (PII risk).

kevin: update: switching kv-cache off reduces hallucination rate by ~65% on the sample run. That's surprising — suggests interaction with KV indexing or position embedding handling during dequant.

maya: that is a huge clue. thanks.

nightly-bot: Logged incident REG-3219: "ellipsis-bleed hallucination regression on rdx-alt-int6-v2". Assigned: maya, kevin, sahil.

lucy: will add failing prompts + golden outputs to the eval harness so nightly can catch this next run. :thumbsup:
